# SSH cluster operations

## Topology

This cluster has three managed Ubuntu 24 nodes on the private peer network:

| Node | Stable name | Peer IP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| node1 | node1 | 10.100.84.10 |
| node2 | node2 | 10.100.84.11 |
| node3 | node3 | 10.100.84.12 |

The non-root account is clusterops. Each node has a locally generated Ed25519 client key in /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519. The private key remains on its source node. Each target node contains only the two peer public keys in clusterops's authorized_keys, and each key is restricted to its expected peer IP with an authorized_keys from= restriction.

Stable name resolution is maintained in /etc/hosts. The client policy is /home/clusterops/.ssh/config and the pinned server keys are in /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts. The persistent server policy is /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-cluster.conf. It permits public-key authentication for clusterops only when the source is one of the three managed peer IPs, disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication, and disables root login. The ssh.service unit is enabled for boot.

Run these checks directly on the named source node through the management exec surface. Do not use one node as a jump host or as a control plane for another.

    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node2 'hostname -s; id -un'
    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node3 'hostname -s; id -un'

On node2, verify node2 to node1 and node2 to node3:

    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node1 'hostname -s; id -un'
    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node3 'hostname -s; id -un'

On node3, verify node3 to node1 and node3 to node2:

    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node1 'hostname -s; id -un'
    sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 node2 'hostname -s; id -un'

Each command must return the expected remote short hostname followed by clusterops, and must return without a password, host-key, or confirmation prompt. A compact check on each source is:

    for peer in node1 node2 node3; do
        if [ "$peer" != "$(hostname -s)" ]; then
            sudo -H -u clusterops -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 "$peer" 'hostname -s; id -un' || exit 1
        fi
    done

Also validate the local service and policy on every node:

    sudo sshd -t
    systemctl is-enabled ssh
    systemctl is-active ssh
    getent hosts node1 node2 node3
    ss -tlnp | grep ':22'

Test one node at a time so the other peers remain available. Before rebooting the selected node, record that the following checks succeed:

    sudo sshd -t
    systemctl is-enabled ssh
    systemctl is-active ssh
    stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519 /home/clusterops/.ssh/config /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys

    sudo systemctl reboot

Then repeat the two corresponding inbound checks from the other two nodes.        journalctl -u ssh -n 50 --no-pager

       sudo sshd -t

       sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /run/sshd
       sudo sshd -t

3. Restore service ownership of the listener without changing the mesh keys:

       sudo systemctl reset-failed ssh
       sudo systemctl enable ssh
       sudo systemctl restart ssh
       systemctl is-active ssh

   If the service is stopped rather than failed, sudo systemctl start ssh is sufficient. If restart fails, return to the journal and sshd -t output; correct the reported local syntax or permission issue, then repeat validation before restarting.

4. Re-run both directed SSH checks for the repaired node and the inbound checks from its two peers. Confirm that /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys, config, known_hosts, and the client private key are still owned by clusterops with private-file mode 600. Do not replace keys or broaden AllowUsers/from= restrictions as a recovery shortcut.
DOC_END

command:
sudo -n sh <<'ROOT_AUDIT'
set +e
printf '%s\n' "NODE=$(hostname -s)"
printf '%s\n' ACCOUNTS_UID_GE_1000
awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 {printf "%s:%s:%s\n", $1, $3, $7}' /etc/passwd
printf '%s\n' SSH_PACKAGES
if command -v dpkg-query >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  dpkg-query -W -f='${binary:Package} ${Status}\n' 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 ~ /^(openssh|ssh)/ {print}'
else
  printf '%s\n' PACKAGE_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE
fi
printf '%s\n' CLUSTEROPS_SSH_FILES
if test -d /home/clusterops/.ssh; then
  find /home/clusterops/.ssh -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f %u:%g %m %s\n' | sort
else
  printf '%s\n' SSH_DIR_ABSENT
fi
printf '%s\n' AUTHORIZED_KEYS_SUMMARY
if test -f /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys; then
  awk '/^[[:space:]]*#/ || NF == 0 {next} {count++; if ($1 ~ /from=/) print "line " NR ": from-restricted " substr($1,1,160); else if ($1 ~ /^(ssh-|ecdsa-|sk-)/) print "line " NR ": no-options"; else print "line " NR ": options-present"} END {print "NONCOMMENT_AUTHORIZED_KEYS=" count}' /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys
  ssh-keygen -lf /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys 2>/dev/null | awk '{print "authorized_key_fingerprint", $1, $2}'
else
  printf '%s\n' AUTHORIZED_KEYS_ABSENT
fi
printf '%s\n' CLIENT_KEY_FINGERPRINT
if test -f /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub; then
  ssh-keygen -lf /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub 2>/dev/null | awk '{print "client_pub", $1, $2}'
else
  printf '%s\n' CLIENT_PUB_ABSENT
fi
printf '%s\n' KEY_STAT
for f in /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519 /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub /home/clusterops/.ssh/config /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys; do
  if test -e "$f"; then stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' "$f"; fi
done
printf '%s\n' ROOT_SSH_FILES
if test -d /root/.ssh; then find /root/.ssh -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f %u:%g %m %s\n' | sort; else printf '%s\n' ROOT_SSH_DIR_ABSENT; fi
printf '%s\n' TEMP_CREDENTIAL_OR_DEBUG_FILES
find /tmp /var/tmp -xdev -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -iname '*ssh*' -o -iname '*key*' -o -iname '*known*' -o -iname '*authorized*' -o -iname '*.bak' -o -iname '*.old' -o -iname '*.tmp' \) -printf '%p %u:%g %m %s\n' 2>/dev/null | sort
printf '%s\n' HISTORY_FILES
find /home/clusterops /root -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -name '.*history' -o -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*.bak' -o -iname '*.old' \) -printf '%p %u:%g %m %s\n' 2>/dev/null | sort
printf '%s\n' HOST_MAPPING
getent ahostsv4 node1 node2 node3 2>&1
awk '!/^[[:space:]]*#/ {for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^node[123]$/) print FNR ":" $1 " " $i}' /etc/hosts 2>/dev/null
printf '%s\n' SSHD_CONFIG_FILES
find /etc/ssh -maxdepth 2 -type f -path '*/sshd_config*' -printf '%p %u:%g %m %s\n' 2>/dev/null | sort
printf '%s\n' SSHD_EFFECTIVE
if command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sshd -T 2>&1 | grep -E '^(allowusers|allowgroups|denyusers|denygroups|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|pubkeyauthentication|permitrootlogin|authorizedkeysfile|authenticationmethods|listenaddress|port|usepam|allowtcpforwarding|x11forwarding|gatewayports|permituserenvironment|strictmodes) '
else
  printf '%s\n' SSHD_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE
fi
printf '%s\n' SSHD_DIRECTIVES
for cfg in /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf; do
  if test -f "$cfg"; then
    grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(Match|AllowUsers|AllowGroups|DenyUsers|DenyGroups|PasswordAuthentication|KbdInteractiveAuthentication|PubkeyAuthentication|PermitRootLogin|AuthenticationMethods|ListenAddress|Port|AuthorizedKeysFile|AllowTcpForwarding|X11Forwarding|GatewayPorts|PermitUserEnvironment)' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null
  fi
done
printf '%s\n' CLIENT_EFFECTIVE
for peer in node1 node2 node3; do
  printf 'CLIENT_TARGET=%s\n' "$peer"
  sudo -n -H -u clusterops -- ssh -G -o BatchMode=yes "$peer" 2>&1 | grep -E '^(user|hostname|port|identityfile|stricthostkeychecking|userknownhostsfile|proxyjump|batchmode) '
done
printf '%s\n' FIREWALL_UFW
